commit_message:
[GlobalOptimazation] Fold empty-set reductions to linalg.fill

Reductions over a zero-sized dimension (e.g. input shape 2x0x4 -> 2x1x4)
lower to a linalg.generic with a 0-extent input, which crashes codegen
tiling (computeAllSliceParameters assertion). Mathematically the result
is the reduction identity broadcast to the output shape (sum -> 0,
prod -> 1).

This adds a pattern in RemoveZeroExtentTensors that folds such reductions
into tensor.empty + linalg.fill(identity), so the 0-extent generic never
reaches codegen.

Fixes 7 onnx_ops *_empty_set cases:
test_reduce_sum_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l1_empty_set
test_reduce_l1_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l2_empty_set
test_reduce_log_sum_exp_empty_set

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimazation] Fold empty-set reductions to linalg.fill

Reductions over a zero-sized dimension (e.g. input shape 2x0x4 -> 2x1x4)
lower to a linalg.generic with a 0-extent input, which crashes codegen
tiling (computeAllSliceParameters assertion). Mathematically the result
is the reduction identity broadcast to the output shape (sum -> 0,
prod -> 1).

This adds a pattern in RemoveZeroExtentTensors that folds such reductions
into tensor.empty + linalg.fill(identity), so the 0-extent generic never
reaches codegen.

[GlobalOptimazation] Fold empty-set reductions to linalg.fill

Reductions over a zero-sized dimension (e.g. input shape 2x0x4 -> 2x1x4)
lower to a linalg.generic with a 0-extent input, which crashes codegen
tiling (computeAllSliceParameters assertion). Mathematically the result
is the reduction identity broadcast to the output shape (sum -> 0,
prod -> 1).

This adds a pattern in RemoveZeroExtentTensors that folds such reductions
into tensor.empty + linalg.fill(identity), so the 0-extent generic never
reaches codegen.

Fixes 7 onnx_ops *_empty_set cases:
test_reduce_sum_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l1_empty_set
test_reduce_l1_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l2_empty_set
test_reduce_log_sum_exp_empty_set

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix O(N²) compile-time scaling in partitionRegionConcurrencyReference

Fix a compile-time regression in Stream partitioning analysis
(`partitionRegionConcurrencyReference`) when processing execution regions
where many operations share a common resource operand (e.g., unrolled or
sliced dispatches sharing an input tensor).

In `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference`, for each operation and resource
operand, all users of the operand were inspected. For each user op, the
pass invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)`. Because `hasAnyTiedUses`
scanned linearly over all use sites of `operand` inside an outer loop over
users, the check scaled cubically/quadratically with the number of dispatches
sharing that resource: O(ops * users * uses).

- Switch from `operand.getUsers()` to `operand.getUses()` in
  `ReferencePartitioning.cpp` to directly inspect each use site with its
  `OpOperand`.
- Replace `hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` (O(uses)) with
  `isOperandTied(use.getOperandNumber())` (O(1)), eliminating the inner scan.
- Add `seenTiedUsers` (`llvm::SmallPtrSet<Operation *, 4>`) to deduplicate
  hazard accumulation when an operation references the operand across
  multiple argument positions.

Signed-off-by: isa-lai <isabellai1004@gmail.com>

commit_message: [GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math (#24902) Rewrites contractions over `iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine` operands into integer contractions, integer zero-point corrections, and floating-point scaling. The transformation uses indexing maps and iterator types to handle named and generic contractions, including convolutions. It reduces in integer arithmetic over dimensions where quantization parameters are invariant. For blockwise quantization, it computes integer partial results, applies each block's correction and scales, then accumulates across blocks in floating point. Zero-point correction terms are built as separate computations so constant terms can be evaluated independently. Corrections are applied before conversion to floating point. Scaling and accumulation use at least f32, preserving wider scale or output types and narrowing only the final result. The rewrite requires a plain multiply-add body, zero initialization, and positive static integer reduction extents whose products and corrections fit in signed i32. Unsupported cases retain the original computation. The pass is enabled by default; reassociation changes floating-point rounding. It can be disabled with `--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false`. Builds on the [affine QDQ operations PR #24901](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24901) and implements the contraction rewrite portion of [Linalg(_ext) native QDQ #24862](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24862). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 --------- Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) Co-authored-by: Florian Walbroel

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

commit_message: [GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math (#24902) Rewrites contractions over `iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine` operands into integer contractions, integer zero-point corrections, and floating-point scaling. The transformation uses indexing maps and iterator types to handle named and generic contractions, including convolutions. It reduces in integer arithmetic over dimensions where quantization parameters are invariant. For blockwise quantization, it computes integer partial results, applies each block's correction and scales, then accumulates across blocks in floating point. Zero-point correction terms are built as separate computations so constant terms can be evaluated independently. Corrections are applied before conversion to floating point. Scaling and accumulation use at least f32, preserving wider scale or output types and narrowing only the final result. The rewrite requires a plain multiply-add body, zero initialization, and positive static integer reduction extents whose products and corrections fit in signed i32. [GlobalOptimazation] Fold empty-set reductions to linalg.fill

Reductions over a zero-sized dimension (e.g. input shape 2x0x4 -> 2x1x4)
lower to a linalg.generic with a 0-extent input, which crashes codegen
tiling (computeAllSliceParameters assertion). Mathematically the result
is the reduction identity broadcast to the output shape (sum -> 0,
prod -> 1).

This adds a pattern in RemoveZeroExtentTensors that folds such reductions
into tensor.empty + linalg.fill(identity), so the 0-extent generic never
reaches codegen.

Fixes 7 onnx_ops *_empty_set cases:
test_reduce_sum_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set
test_reduce_sum_square_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l1_empty_set
test_reduce_l1_empty_set_expanded
test_reduce_l2_empty_set
test_reduce_log_sum_exp_empty_set
